manifest_add_item.title: Two cyclotomic shears give a periodic integrable based quantum sl-two chain

manifest_add_item.statement:
Put $K=\mathbb Q(q)$, $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$, $p=q+q^{-1}$ and $h=q^2+q^{-2}$. For $k\ge0$ set

$$n_{2k}=8k+2,\qquad n_{2k+1}=8k+4,\qquad \ell_{2k}=2,\qquad\ell_{2k+1}=4,\qquad r_j=\ell_j-1,$$

and set $p_j=p$ for even $j$ and $p_j=h$ for odd $j$. Let $u_{j,a}=F^{(a)}u_{j,0}$, $0\le a\le n_j$, be the divided basis of the highest string $V(n_j)$, of weight $n_j-2a$. On the algebraic module $M=\bigoplus_{j\ge0}V(n_j)$ define

$$T_j u_{j,t\ell_j}=(-1)^t u_{j+1,r_j+t\ell_j}\quad(0\le t\le n_j/\ell_j),$$

and define $T_j$ to be zero on all other divided basis vectors. Put $S=\sum_jT_j/p_j$, $C=1+S$, and $b_{j,a}=C u_{j,a}$.

Then $S^2=0$ and $C^{-1}=1-S$; these are finite-column algebraic operators. The homogeneous basis $B=\{b_{j,a}\}$ has a free $U_A$-stable integral span, its standard compatible bar fixes $B$, and its regular zero and infinity charts and crystal residues are those of the standard direct sum of divided strings. Thus it is an actual four-axiom based integrable finite-Cartan-type module, with a balanced integral triple and no choice assumption.

For every $J\ge0$, the finite version $M^{(J)}=\bigoplus_{0\le j\le J}V(n_j)$, with shears only for $j<J$, has the same properties. For every $a\in U_A$ the raw-coordinate action is $C^{-1}aC=a+[a,S]-SaS$; its column at a raw basis vector of index $j$ is supported at summand indices at most $j+2$. That column agrees with the finite version whenever $J\ge j+2$.

The raw seed $b_{0,0}\otimes b_{0,2}$ in two copies has total weight zero and factor weights $2,-2$. Both factors are deformed: $b_{0,0}=u_{0,0}+u_{1,1}/p$ and $b_{0,2}=u_{0,2}-u_{1,3}/p$. This statement constructs the modules and finite versions; it does not assert infinite tensor correction supports.

citations.quote:
Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$, an index $i\in I$, and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra and let $A_i$ be the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]); write $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$ for the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

(i) The assignment $e\mapsto E_i$, $f\mapsto F_i$, $k\mapsto K_i$, $k^{-1}\mapsto K_i^{-1}$ defines an algebra isomorphism from the standard rank-one algebra $\mathbb A$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$, presented by $e,f,k^{\pm1}$ with $kek^{-1}=q_i^2e$, $kfk^{-1}=q_i^{-2}f$ and $[e,f]=(k-k^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ onto $A_i$; the images of the monomials $F_i^aK_i^mE_i^b$ ($a,b\ge0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$) are linearly independent in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, being images of the PBW monomials of the triangular decomposition ([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

(ii) For all $a,b\ge0$, $K_iE_i^{(a)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{2a}E_i^{(a)}$ and $K_iF_i^{(b)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2b}F_i^{(b)}$, and for $b\ge1$ the divided powers satisfy the exact commutation formula
$$E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+\frac{F_i^{(b-1)}}{q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1}\bigr);$$
iterating it computes $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ as a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ ($0\le t\le\min(a,b)$) with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$.

(iii) For every $N\ge0$ there is a simple $A_i$-module $L_i(N)$ of dimension $N+1$: it is the quotient of the cyclic module $\widetilde M(N):=A_i/\bigl(A_iE_i+A_i(K_i-q_i^N)\bigr)$ by the submodule generated by $F_i^{(N+1)}w_N$, where $w_N$ is the image of $1$, with basis the images $v_t$ of $F_i^{(t)}w_N$, $0\le t\le N$, on which $K_iv_t=q_i^{N-2t}v_t$, $F_iv_t=[t+1]_iv_{t+1}$ and $E_iv_t=[N-t+1]_iv_{t-1}$ (with $v_{-1}=v_{N+1}=0$); $L_i(N)$ is the unique simple $A_i$-module generated by a vector $v\ne0$ with $E_iv=0$, $K_iv=q_i^Nv$ and $F_i^{N+1}v=0$.

Fix $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\subseteq\mathbb Q(q)$ and the crystal limiting ring $A_0\subseteq\mathbb Q(q)$ of [[def-the-local-ring-at-q-zero]], and put $A_\infty:=\psi(A_0)$, the image of $A_0$ under the semilinear involution $\psi(q)=q^{-1}$, i.e. the ring of rational functions regular at $q=\infty$; $A_0$ and $A_\infty$ are the rational local rings at $0$ and at infinity, and the integral affine chart coordinate rings are $\mathbb Z[q]$ and $\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]$.

Let $M$ be one of $U_q^-$ or $V(\lambda)=L(\lambda)$ for $\lambda\in P^+$. Equip $M$ with the bar involution $\psi$ of [[lem-the-lusztig-integral-form-is-stable-under-bar-and-contravariant-duality]]: on $U_q^-$ the semilinear algebra involution with $\psi(q)=q^{-1}$, $\psi(E_i)=E_i$, $\psi(F_i)=F_i$, $\psi(K_h)=K_h^{-1}$; on $V(\lambda)$ the induced semilinear involution determined by $Pv_\lambda\mapsto\psi(P)v_\lambda$, well defined by the highest-module presentation: its negative-half kernel is $\sum_iU_q^-F_i^{\lambda(h_i)+1}$, preserved by $\psi$ because every $F_i$ is fixed ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]). Equivalently the full highest-vector relations are bar stable: $E_i$ is fixed, the singular divided powers are fixed, and $\psi(K_h-q^{\langle\lambda,h\rangle})=-q^{-\langle\lambda,h\rangle}K_{-h}(K_h-q^{\langle\lambda,h\rangle})$. Hence the quotient involution is compatible with the algebra action and fixes $v_\lambda$. Let $M_A\subseteq M$ be the divided-power integral form: $M_A=U_A^-$ for $M=U_q^-$, and $M_A=V_A(\lambda):=U_A^-v_\lambda$ for $M=V(\lambda)$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]); both are $\psi$-stable. Let $L$ be the Kashiwara crystal lattice of $M$ over $A_0$: $L=\mathcal L(\infty)$ for $U_q^-$ and $L=\mathcal L(\lambda)$ for $V(\lambda)$ ([[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], [[thm-grand-loop-existence-of-highest-weight-crystal-bases]]).

Define the **bar lattice** $L^-:=\psi(L)$, an $A_\infty$-submodule of $M$, and the **balanced part** $E:=M_A\cap L\cap L^-$.

The definition keeps three structures on the same $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space strictly separate: the $A$-module $M_A$, which is not assumed free and not claimed to be contained in $L$; the free $A_0$-module $L$; and the free $A_\infty$-module $L^-$. No equality $L^-=L$, no inclusion $M_A\subseteq L$, no freeness of $M_A$ and no identification $E=M_A$ are asserted; freeness is a conclusion of the balanced-triple construction on this page, whereas $E$ is a $\mathbb Z$-module of global lifts and is not equal to the Laurent lattice $M_A$. The bar lattice is not the form-dual (upper) lattice, which is defined later on this page. The intersections $M_A\cap L$ and $M_A\cap L^-$ are respectively $\mathbb Z[q]$- and $\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]$-modules, generally not $A$-modules. The balanced part $E$ is a $\mathbb Z$-module; its Laurent extension $A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E$ is the full integral module once globalization is proved.

More generally a **based integrable module** $(M,B)$ here means exactly: $B$ is a homogeneous field basis; $M_A=\bigoplus_bAb$ is $U_A$-stable; the semilinear involution fixing $B$ is compatible with the algebra action; and $L_0=\bigoplus_bA_0b$ with residue $B$ is a crystal local basis at $0$. These are the four conditions of Lusztig 27.1.2(a)–(d) after the transport $v=q^{-1}$, together with the integrable extension used by Bao–Wang. Such data do not automatically imply an integral $\Theta$-action on an arbitrary based pair. A **based subobject** is a $U$-submodule spanned by a subset of $B$; a **based quotient** is its quotient with the complementary basis images. Based morphisms send $B$ to the target basis or to $0$, and have kernels spanned by the killed basis subset. These exact integral and bar-compatible maps, not arbitrary field summands, are used in tensor inheritance.

For every $n\ge1$ the cyclotomic polynomial $\Phi_n$
([[def-cyclotomic-polynomial]]) is irreducible in $\mathbb Q[t]$
([[def-irreducible-and-prime-elements-in-a-domain]]).

The Laurent polynomial ring $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$ of
[[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]] is Noetherian, hence every ideal of
$\Lambda$ is finitely generated, and $\Lambda$ is a unique factorisation
domain; its units are $\pm t^k$, $k\in\mathbb Z$, and $t$ is prime in $\mathbb Z[t]$ but becomes a unit in $\Lambda$.

derivations.claim: **The two denominators and the weights.** One has $p=q^{-1}\Phi_4$ and $h=q^{-2}\Phi_8$, so [F2] makes them nonassociate prime elements of $A$. Both are bar fixed, and $1/p=q/(1+q^2)$ and $1/h=q^2/(1+q^4)$ belong to $qA_0$ and, by bar invariance, to $q^{-1}A_\infty$. The source highest weight $n_j$ is divisible by $\ell_j$, and $n_{j+1}=n_j+2r_j$ for both parities. Hence every displayed target has the same weight as its source and lies in the target string.

**All the modular Gaussian coefficients.** For $\ell\in\{2,4\}$ reduce modulo $q^{-\ell/2}\Phi_{2\ell}(q)$, which is the corresponding $p_j$. Then $z=q^2$ has order $\ell$ and $q^\ell=-1$. The generating identity $\prod_{a=0}^{N-1}(1+z^aX)=\sum_t z^{t(t-1)/2}\binom Nt_zX^t$ follows by multiplication and the Gaussian recurrence; each full block of length $\ell$ is $1-(-X)^\ell$. It follows that a Gaussian coefficient with lower remainder larger than upper remainder modulo $\ell$ vanishes. For $r=\ell-1$ and $t\ge0$, the coefficient $\binom{r+t}{t}_{q}$ vanishes unless $t=v\ell$; in that case its unsymmetrized Gaussian value is $1$ and its symmetrizing factor is $q^{-v\ell(\ell-1)}=(-1)^v$, since $\ell$ is even. This gives exactly the coefficients of $T_j$ modulo $p_j$. All reductions are in the integral domain $A/(p_j)$, so they are divisibilities in $A$.

**Full divided-power intertwining modulo each denominator.** Fix $j$, put $n=n_j=a\ell_j$, $r=\ell_j-1$ and $m=n+2r$, and take $v=u_{j+1,r}$ in $V_A(m)/(p_j)$. Its weight is $n$. For $1\le t\le r$, the coefficient of $E^{(t)}v$ is $\binom{(a+1)\ell_j-1+t}{t}_q$, with upper remainder $t-1$ and lower remainder $t$, so it vanishes by step 2.1; larger $t$ give zero by the endpoint. Also $F^{(t)}v$ vanishes for every $t>n$: until $t=(a+1)\ell_j-1$ its nonzero remainder forces vanishing by step 2.1, and larger $t$ exceed the target endpoint. The assignment $u_{j,t}\mapsto F^{(t)}v$ therefore intertwines all divided $F$ actions by Gaussian multiplication. Divided $E$ reordering, using the annihilation of all positive divided $E$ powers on the weight-$n$ vector $v$, gives exactly $\binom{n-t+s}{s}_q F^{(t-s)}v$ for $E^{(s)}F^{(t)}v$, including zero beyond the source endpoints. Toral elements act by matched weight scalars. Step 2.1 identifies this assignment with $T_j$ modulo $p_j$, proving $[a,T_j]V_A(n_j)\subseteq p_jV_A(n_{j+1})$ for every $a\in U_A$.

**Algebraic invertibility and integral cross terms.** Every $T_j$ is supported on even positions and has odd target positions. Thus $T_{j+1}T_j=0$ exactly, and all other twofold products vanish by their summand indices. Every column is finite, so $S^2=0$ and $C^{-1}=1-S$ on the algebraic direct sum. For $a\in U_A$, expansion gives $C^{-1}aC=a+[a,S]-SaS$. The commutator summands are integral by step 3.1. The only cross terms are $T_{j+1}aT_j/(p_{j+1}p_j)$. Their numerators are divisible by $p_j$, using $T_{j+1}(aT_j-T_ja)$, and by $p_{j+1}$, using $(T_{j+1}a-aT_{j+1})T_j$. Adjacent denominators are the two distinct primes of step 1.1, so their product divides every matrix entry by [F2]. The conjugated operator therefore preserves the standard free integral span, proving stability of the $B$-span. No nonadjacent repeated denominator creates a cross term.

**The compatible basis and crystal charts.** The inverse in step 4.1 proves that $B$ is a field basis with free integral span; its homogeneity is step 1.1. The coefficients $(-1)^t/p_j$ are bar fixed, so the standard module bar fixes $B$ and remains compatible with the algebra action. The module is integrable because every vector occupies finitely many finite standard strings. By step 1.1, $C$ and its inverse preserve both regular charts and are the identity on both residues, so the charts and crystal vertices coincide with the standard direct-sum ones. Their Kashiwara operators are exactly the finite shifts in [F1]. Thus all four conditions of [F3] hold.

**Balancedness, finite versions and exact column agreement.** In the common basis $B$, the three coefficient rings are $A,A_0,A_\infty$; their simultaneous intersection is $\mathbb Z$ and $A\cap A_0=\mathbb Z[q]$, since a Laurent polynomial regular at both ends is constant. Coefficientwise reduction therefore gives the integral balanced isomorphism, with finite support throughout. Omitting shears at indices at least $J$ preserves every preceding argument and gives the stated finite version. A standard action $a$ preserves each constituent summand; $C$ can raise the constituent index by at most one and $C^{-1}$ by at most one. Thus the raw column of $C^{-1}aC$ at index $j$ has indices at most $j+2$ and uses only shears with index at most $j+1$, all present when $J\ge j+2$; its finite and infinite computations agree. Finally the signs at positions $0,2$ in the first string give exactly the two stated seed formulas and factor weights. Every vector, map and index is specified explicitly, so no choice is used.

manifest_add_item.title: Actual terminal dot caps have a prefix residue formula

references.title: Ben Webster, Knot invariants and higher representation theory I, arXiv:1001.2020v9
references.locator: Proposition 1.7, printed pp.17–19, transports the partial adjunctions; Theorem 1.8 and Figure 6, printed pp.19–22, motivate the terminal quadratic contraction. The actual arbitrary-prefix residue identification and two-return contraction are proved here.

manifest_add_item.statement:
Fix a real symmetrizable KLR datum over a degree-zero field $k$, every
homogeneous (Q1)–(Q4) parameter family, a dominant framing $\Lambda$, and the
standard first-strand cyclotomic quotient. More generally let $a_i(z)$ be
any monic field specialization of degree
$\lambda_i=\langle h_i,\Lambda\rangle$, using the ungraded monic quotient.
Let $A=R_a^\Lambda(\gamma)$, let $\eta=(\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_n)$ have root
weight $\gamma$, and put $h_i=\langle h_i,\Lambda-\gamma\rangle$ and
$q_{ij}(z,x)=Q_{ij}(z,x)/t_{ij}$ for $i\ne j$.
The maps $T_i^\gamma$ are the actual regular-module second counits constructed
in [[lem-cyclotomic-klr-induction-restriction-bimodules-have-compatible-frobenius-dual-bases]],
with its canonical first-adjoint identification and ordinary first unit.
Define the formal Laurent expansion at infinity
$$R_i^\eta(z)=\frac{\prod_{a:\eta_a=i}(z-x_a)^2}{a_i(z)\prod_{a:\eta_a\ne i}q_{i\eta_a}(z,x_a)}\in e(\eta)Ae(\eta)((z^{-1})).$$
Every denominator is expanded by its monic leading coefficient; its
coefficients are polynomials in the old dots. Then for every integer $m\ge0$,
$$T_i^\gamma(e(\eta i)x_{n+1}^m)=e(\eta)[z^{-1}]z^mR_i^\eta(z).$$
The associated series coefficients, collected over all $\eta$ of weight
$\gamma$, are central in $A$.

For distinct $i,j$, take $u,v$ to label respectively the $i,j$ terminal dots,
and let $g\in(e(\eta)Ae(\eta))[u,v]$, with coefficients placed on the left.
Use the right-append homomorphisms to evaluate its coefficients. Relabel
$u,v$ in the $\eta ji$ corner by color, so that $u=x_{n+2}$ and $v=x_{n+1}$
there. Both following compositions are actual maps to $e(\eta)Ae(\eta)$:
$$T_i^\gamma T_j^{\gamma+\alpha_i}\big(e(\eta ij)Q_{ij}(u,v)g(u,v)\big)=t_{ji}\mathcal D_\eta(g),$$
$$T_j^\gamma T_i^{\gamma+\alpha_j}\big(e(\eta ji)Q_{ji}(v,u)g(u,v)\big)=t_{ij}\mathcal D_\eta(g),$$
where a common residual map is explicitly
$$\mathcal D_\eta(g)=[u^{-1}v^{-1}]g(u,v)R_i^\eta(u)R_j^\eta(v).$$
These identities include arbitrary downward prefixes, all input weights and
zero corners. They establish the two-return terminal quadratic contraction.
They do not identify the residual maps of the zero-return or one-return
terminal patterns. In the homogeneous standard case the cap has degree
$2d_i(1-h_i)$; arbitrary monic specializations assert the ungraded formulas.

citations.quote:
For the standard first-strand cyclotomic quotient of a real symmetrizable KLR
datum over any degree-zero field and every homogeneous (Q1)–(Q4) parameter
family, put $A=R^\Lambda(\beta)$, $B=R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)$,
$e=e(\beta,i)$, $X=Be$, $Y=eB$,
$h=\langle h_i,\Lambda-\beta\rangle$ and $t=2d_i(1-h)$.
There are explicit, compatible homogeneous maps
$$T_i:eBe\longrightarrow A,\qquad \deg T_i=t,$$
and finite homogeneous tensors
$$C_i=\sum_\alpha x_\alpha\otimes_A y_\alpha\in X\otimes_A Y,\qquad \deg x_\alpha+\deg y_\alpha=-t,$$
such that $T_i$ is an $A$-bimodule map, $bC_i=C_ib$ for every $b\in B$, and
$$x=\sum_\alpha x_\alpha T_i(y_\alpha x),\qquad y=\sum_\alpha T_i(yx_\alpha)y_\alpha.$$
In particular $X\{t\}\cong\operatorname{HOM}_A(Y,A)$ as $(B,A)$-bimodules,
where Hom is left-$A$-linear, the left $B$-action is precomposition with
right multiplication on $Y$, and the right $A$-action is multiplication on
values. The second unit is $b\mapsto bC_i$ and the second counit is
$y\otimes_B x\mapsto T_i(yx)$, giving
$E_i\{t\}\dashv F_i\dashv E_i$ on all graded modules. They are obtained by
finite normal-form/cap transport, not by assuming an actual Frobenius trace.
Dots and same-color crossing mates have the native cyclic normalization.
Each specified distinguished-$i$ different-color sideways pair has both
composites $t_{ij}$ times the identity. The separately distinguished-$j$
construction has both composites $t_{ji}$ times the identity. These are
different partial actions, not two different scalar values for the two
orders of one pair; their full word-closure comparison is not inferred here.
Arbitrary monic field specializations have the same ungraded construction,
with grading shifts forgotten. No finite-type, characteristic-zero,
geometric-global-basis or symmetric-trace premise is used.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum with real simple roots (so $a_{ii}=2$ for
every color $i$), a field $k$ placed in degree zero, and weighted-homogeneous
KLR polynomials $Q_{jk}$ satisfying (Q1)-(Q4) as in
[[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]; write
$b_{jk}=d_j a_{jk}=b_{kj}$. Fix a color $i$. The **minimal-parabolic KLR
diagram proof category** $\mathcal P_i$ is the additive graded $k$-linear
2-category of weighted oriented diagrams described by the generators, objects
and equations below.

**Generators and composition.** The objects are the weights
$\mu\in P$. The generating $1$-morphisms are the downward generators
$G_j:\mu\to\mu-\alpha_j$, one for every color $j$, and the single upward
generator $H_i:\mu\to\mu+\alpha_i$. Horizontal composition reads chronological
negative words from the vacuum outward. Take additive sums of objects and
grading shifts, and use idempotent completion when speaking of word
projectives. The generator $H_i$ denotes **normalized projective
restriction**: in the polynomial flag realization at input weight $h=\langle
h_i,\mu\rangle$ it is basic reversed flag restriction shifted by
$-d_i(1+h)$; it is distinct from unshifted basic restriction.

**The graded 2-morphism spaces.** The weights are 0-objects. A 1-morphism
is a finite composable word in the $G_j,H_i$, with its specified source and
target weights; identities are empty words. For parallel words $u,v$, define
$\operatorname{Hom}^n(u,v)$ as the degree-$n$ part of the $k$-span of formal
oriented string diagrams generated by the dots, downward crossings and four
units/counits below, modulo the displayed local relations. Every strand is
labeled by its color, and its direction is downward for $G_j$ and upward for
$H_i$. The top boundary is the source word and the bottom boundary the target
word. Regions carry the unique weights obtained from the outside source
weight by the indicated simple-root changes. Diagrams are generic: transverse
double crossings, isolated dots and nondegenerate cups/caps, with no triple
crossing or dot at a crossing/extremum. Oppositely oriented crossings denote
the specified adjunction mates of a downward crossing, not new generators.
Use planar isotopies preserving the ordered oriented local events; moving
a crossing past an extremum uses the mate relations below. Vertical
composition is stacking and horizontal composition is juxtaposition at a
common weight; degrees add under either operation. The interchange relation
and bilinearity are imposed. A degree-$n$ map from $u$ to $v$ is a degree-zero
map $u\{n\}\to v$ with the internal-shift convention of the grading supplier.
Additive sums, shifts and idempotent completion have their usual graded
2-category meanings applied to these Hom spaces.

**Degrees and the native crossing.** Dots have degree $2d_j$ and downward
crossings have degree $-b_{jk}$, matching the grading of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]. The native crossing is
$\tau$, with native equal-color divided difference
$(f-sf)/(x_1-x_2)$; for expressing the source diagram equations put
$\kappa=-\tau$ for **every** color pair, retaining dots, idempotents and $Q$.
Thus the native cubic braid numerator is globally opposite to the source
numerator, while the quadratic $Q$ is unchanged. Impose the full downward KLR
relations of the cited Definition.

**Adjunctions and the rank-one matrix.** At input $i$-weight $h$, the first
unit $1\to H_iG_i$ and the second counit $H_iG_i\to1$ have degree
$d_i(1-h)$; the first counit $G_iH_i\to1$ and the second unit
$1\to G_iH_i$ have degree $d_i(1+h)$. Impose both adjunction triangles with
their adjacent input-weight shifts and cyclicity of the dot. For $h\ge0$
prescribe the degree-zero rank-one matrix
$$H_iG_i\cong G_iH_i\oplus\bigoplus_{r=0}^{h-1}1\{d_i(1-h+2r)\};$$
for $h<0$ prescribe
$$G_iH_i\cong H_iG_i\oplus\bigoplus_{r=0}^{-h-1}1\{d_i(1+h+2r)\}.$$
The off-diagonal crossing component is the cup--source-crossing--cap
transfer, and the identity columns and rows are the indicated dotted
units/counits. Adjoin its actual inverse blocks, requiring both matrix inverse
equations; the dotted dual rows and columns are the finite triangular
coefficient convolution determined by bubble inversion, and the crossing
block satisfies the local cross-and-cap equations. In particular, at $h<0$,
if $r_h:G_iH_i\to H_iG_i\oplus D_{-h}$ is this matrix, then $r_h^{-1}j_H$ and
$p_Hr_h$ are the specified natural inclusion and projection with product
$1_{H_iG_i}$.

**Explicit rank-one inverse blocks.** Put $P=G_iH_i$, $V=H_iG_i$
at the common outside weight $\mu$, and write
$\eta_\mu:1_\mu\to H_iG_i$, $\varepsilon_\mu:G_iH_i\to1_\mu$
for the first adjunction and
$\eta'_\mu:1_\mu\to G_iH_i$, $\varepsilon'_\mu:H_iG_i\to1_\mu$
for the second. Let $\tau^{GG}$ be the native equal-color downward crossing
and $\tau^{HH}$ its twofold adjunction mate. Fix the native sideways mates by
$$T=(H_iG_i\varepsilon_\mu)(H_i\tau^{GG}H_i)(\eta_\mu G_iH_i),\qquad S=(G_iH_i\varepsilon'_\mu)(G_i\tau^{HH}G_i)(\eta'_\mu H_iG_i).$$
Their middle words are respectively $H_iG_iG_iH_i$ and

$$R^-_k=\sum_{a+j=-h-1-k}\mathsf H_{\mu,j}\,\varepsilon_\mu x^a,\qquad 0\le k<-h,$$

reciprocal coefficient is defined by the finite recursion with constant
coefficient $1$.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum with finite color set $I$ and no imaginary
simple roots, a KLR datum $Q=(Q_{ij})_{i\ne j}$ satisfying (Q1)-(Q4), and a
field $k$ placed in degree zero
([[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]],
[[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]); let
$R=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}R(\beta)$ be the resulting graded KLR algebra, with
its idempotents $e(\nu)$, dots $x_a$, crossings $\tau_a$ and degrees
$\deg x_a=2d_{\nu_a}$, $\deg\tau_a=-b_{\nu_a\nu_{a+1}}$
([[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]). Let $\Lambda$ be a
dominant integral weight and put $\lambda_i:=\langle h_i,\Lambda\rangle\ge0$
([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]).

**Cyclotomic data.** For every color $i$ choose a monic polynomial
$a_i(u)\in k[u]$ of degree exactly $\lambda_i$
([[def-polynomial-ring-over-a-commutative-ring]]); the standard choice made
below is $a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}$. For $n\ge1$ write
$$a(x_s)=\sum_{\nu\in I^n}a_{\nu_s}(x_s)e(\nu)\qquad(1\le s\le n),$$
the element of $R_n(Q)$ that acts on the $\nu$-component by the monic
polynomial $a_{\nu_s}$ in the dot at position $s$.

**The cyclotomic quotient.** For $\beta\in Q_+$ define $J_a(\beta)$ to be the
two-sided ideal of $R(\beta)$ generated by the first-strand elements
$a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)$, $\nu\in I^\beta$; equivalently
$$J_a(\beta)=\sum_{\nu\in I^\beta}R(\beta)\,a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)\,R(\beta),$$
and put
$$R_a^\Lambda(\beta):=R(\beta)/J_a(\beta),\qquad R_a^\Lambda(0):=k .$$
The **cyclotomic KLR algebra** is the direct sum
$R_a^\Lambda:=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}R_a^\Lambda(\beta)$; it carries the
local units $e(\beta)=\sum_{\nu\in I^\beta}e(\nu)$, which act as the identity
on $R_a^\Lambda(\beta)$ and annihilate the other summands, and it is a
$k$-algebra with these orthogonal idempotents.

**Standard choice and grading.** The STANDARD choice $a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}$ is
used throughout the graded categorification, duality-normalization and based
statements below; for it we write $R^\Lambda:=R^\Lambda_a$. Under the standard
choice each individual first-strand generator
$x_1^{\lambda_{\nu_1}}e(\nu)$ is homogeneous of degree
$2d_{\nu_1}\lambda_{\nu_1}$ in the grading of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]], so the ideal $J_a(\beta)$
and the quotient $R^\Lambda(\beta)$ are graded, and $R^\Lambda$ is a
$\mathbb Z$-graded algebra with local units. The sum $a(x_1)$ itself need not
have one common degree across different colors, and no single degree is
assigned to it.

coefficients in degree-zero $k$ give an UNGRADED deformation $R_a^\Lambda$;

identification are not asserted for that branch, and the ungraded branch is
used only where a statement explicitly says so. Finite dimension, finite root
strings, ordinary projectivity and symmetry of the standard quotient have the
separately stated monic conclusions below. The cyclotomic relation is imposed
on the FIRST strand, and cyclotomic induction appends strands on the RIGHT
([[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]]); this convention
fixes the side on which the quotient map acts throughout the page.

derivations.claim: Actual cap and index. Apply the ordinary first unit to $e(\eta)$ and decorate its appended strand with $m$ dots; the resulting element is $e(\eta i)x_{n+1}^m$. The canonical first-adjoint transport preserves that unit by [F1]. Its actual second counit consequently evaluates this element as the transported diagram $\varepsilon'_\mu x^m\eta_\mu$, with $\mu=\Lambda-\gamma$. This is the counterclockwise bubble of [F2], hence $e(\eta)\mathsf H_{\eta,m-h_i+1}$. This calculation identifies the constructed $T_i^\gamma$ itself; it does not replace it by a chosen coefficient functional. Negative indices give zero, and no sign or weight shift is omitted: the literal-dot index is $m-h_i+1$, and its degree is $2d_i(m-h_i+1)=2d_im+\deg T_i^\gamma$.

Slide through the prefix. Starting with the vacuum value in [F2], slide the bubble through the chronological letters of $\eta$. Each coefficient computation is finite because every reversed monic factor has constant coefficient one. The resulting series is $\mathsf H_\eta(t)=\prod_{a:\eta_a=i}(1-x_at)^2/(a_i^{\mathrm{rev}}(t)\prod_{a:\eta_a\ne i}q_{i\eta_a}^{\mathrm{rev}}(x_a,t))$. The numerator has degree $2\#\{a:\eta_a=i\}$ in $z$, the denominator has degree $\lambda_i+\sum_{a:\eta_a\ne i}(-a_{i\eta_a})$, and their difference is $-h_i$. Therefore $R_i^\eta(z)=z^{-h_i}\mathsf H_\eta(z^{-1})$. Extracting coefficient $z^{-1}$ from $z^mR_i^\eta(z)$ extracts precisely index $m-h_i+1$ from $\mathsf H_\eta$. Combined with step 1.1 this proves the actual terminal-dot formula, without restriction on the sign of $h_i$.

Centrality and old algebra factors. For an equal-color adjacent pair in $\eta$, the two factors of $\mathsf H_\eta$ are symmetric in their dot variables, so each coefficient commutes with its crossing by [F3]. For a distinct-color pair, swapping the color-variable pairs sends the coefficient in the $\eta$ summand to the coefficient in the swapped-word summand; its crossing has precisely that dot-permutation relation with no correction. Thus the finite sum of these coefficients over the words commutes with every crossing, every dot and every idempotent, which generate $A$. They are central. Appended terminal dots commute with all old generators. For any $b\in e(\eta)Ae(\eta)$, [F1] consequently evaluates $\iota_i(b)e(\eta i)x_{n+1}^m$ as $b\,e(\eta)[z^{-1}]z^mR_i^\eta(z)$. By linearity this identifies the actual cap on every polynomial terminal with arbitrary old algebra coefficients.

First actual quadratic contraction. Put the $i$ dot $u$ on the appended prefix $\eta i$. Its actual terminal-$j$ formula of step 2.1 uses $R_j^{\eta i}(v)=t_{ji}R_j^\eta(v)/Q_{ji}(v,u)$. In this identity the inverse is expanded at infinity in $v$ and has polynomial coefficients in $u$ and the old dots. Apply step 3.1 termwise to the polynomial $Q_{ij}(u,v)g(u,v)$: its old coefficients lie in the append image of $A[u]$. Since $Q_{ij}(u,v)=Q_{ji}(v,u)$, the denominator cancels in the Laurent series before taking the coefficient. The actual inner cap therefore gives $t_{ji}[v^{-1}]g(u,v)R_j^\eta(v)$. This is a polynomial in $u$ with old algebra coefficients: $g$ has finitely many powers of $u,v$, and only finitely many series coefficients contribute to $v^{-1}$. Apply the actual outer $i$ cap by step 3.1. The result is $t_{ji}[u^{-1}][v^{-1}]g(u,v)R_j^\eta(v)R_i^\eta(u)$.

Second contraction and common map. Interchange $i,j$ and keep the variables labeled by color. Now the inner $i$ cap uses $R_i^{\eta j}(u)=t_{ij}R_i^\eta(u)/Q_{ij}(u,v)$, giving $t_{ij}[v^{-1}][u^{-1}]g(u,v)R_i^\eta(u)R_j^\eta(v)$ after the outer $j$ cap. Following the quadratic cancellation, each series depends on only its own terminal variable and the old commuting dots. Their coefficients commute with one another. On the finite polynomial $g$, both extractions use finitely many coefficients and therefore commute. The result of step 4.1 and this result are respectively $t_{ji}\mathcal D_\eta(g)$ and $t_{ij}\mathcal D_\eta(g)$ in the same old algebra corner.
